title: Temporal Topology Saturation Scale: Cross-Scale Consistency of ρ_T
abstract:
Gravitational anomalies across astrophysical scales exhibit an empirical regularity: the radius at which Newtonian dynamics fails scales as R ∝ M¹/3 in the compact saturation regime and R ∝ M¹/2 in the low-acceleration galactic regime, organized by a candidate saturation/proximity density scale ρ_T in the Temporal Equivalence Principle (TEP) conformal time-field sector. The 25-year GNSS atomic-clock correlation length L_c ≈ 4,200 km (CODE, IGS, ESA; raw-RINEX validated) establishes an Earth-scale correlation structure consistent with R_T(M_⊕) = (3M_⊕/4πρ_T)¹/3 = 4,146 km at ρ_T ≈ 20 g/cm³ (ρ_T ∈ [8, 70] g/cm³ conditional mapping under L_c ↔ R_T(M_⊕)). A 4-layer PREM Earth boundary-value integration confirms an order-unity geometric projection (L_c^PREM = 4,010 km shell; 3,213 km volume) governed by Earth's R_CMB and R_⊕ structure, while Monte Carlo network injection–recovery simulations across L_c^true ∈ [1,000, 6,000] km demonstrate that 1-constellation GPS-only processing recovers L_c^true = 4,200 km (L̂_c^GPS = 4,036 ± 113 km; white-noise null |C(d)| = 0.009; correlated orbital/datum dipole null concave-down with d²C/dd² < 0), whereas 4-constellation multi-GNSS inter-system-bias (ISB) projection compresses the same field to L̂_c^MGEX = 2,277 ± 47 km per-epoch (1.77×) and 2,485 ± 45 km daily-constant (1.62×, reproducing the direction and approximate magnitude of the observed 1.90× MGEX offset).

Because the canonical terrestrial BVP is shaped by Earth's fixed geometry, quantitative calibration of ρ_T ≈ 20 g/cm³ rests on direct R_⊕-free cross-mass tests, separated from structural-exponent tests. Direct tests comprise the RBH-1 crossover (M_× = √(3c⁶/(32πG³ρ_T)) ≈ 3.04 × 10⁷ M_⊙, R_T/R_S = 1.32), the zero-parameter equatorial rotation relation v_eq/c = u_T(M)/√(u_gal) (v_gal = 220 km s⁻¹), which matches Earth, Uranus, Neptune, and Saturn at v_obs/v_TEP = 1.016 ± 0.073 (ρ_T^spin = 20.9 g/cm³ geometric mean; extending above M_cap = 194 M_⊕ = 0.61 M_Jup with one small-body capacity parameter η_0 = 0.129 [or the parameter-free secular stability fraction η_sec = 1/8 = 0.125] and S_A = min[1, S] matches Jupiter at -2.9% [-0.2% at η_sec], the fastest planetary-mass rotator SIMP J0136 at -2.8% [-0.3%], and the 1.15 ± 0.08 hr brown-dwarf period floor of Tannock et al. 2021 at P_min^TEP = (k_MOI/η_0)τ_T = 1.17 hr [1.21 hr at η_sec], giving v_obs/v_2br = 1.008 ± 0.060 and ρ_T^rot = 21.1 g/cm³ across N = 9 planetary and substellar systems), and cold-planet moments of inertia k_MOI ≃ (1/2)S (ρ_T^MOI,terr = 17.9 ± 1.4 g/cm³ across the three core-screened terrestrial planets; 2k_MOI/S = 1.17 ± 0.14 across eight planets with a systematic trend toward 8–9 g/cm³ in compressible gas giants). Structural and scale-cancellation tests comprise the SPARC onset scaling (α_SPARC = 0.352 ± 0.043 discrete, N = 168; α_res = 0.417 ± 0.050 on n = 75 resolved crossings compatible with a transition between the M¹/3 saturation and M¹/2 low-acceleration kinetic scales; Tobit rejection of R_DM/R_d invariance at +0.323 ± 0.034, z = 9.57, p < 10⁻⁴; fixed-radius non-circular partial r(R_DM, V_bar(2.2R_d)|R_d) = +0.547, p = 3.8 × 10⁻⁷), the two-branch RAR/BTFR profile P_,X = k√ξ + 2ξ (0.139–0.152 dex RMS on the quality-controlled SPARC sample), the Milky Way onset (3.1 ± 0.4 kpc mean; [1.0, 9.4] kpc 1σ interval), the algebraic S ∝ ρ⁰.334 hierarchy (R² = 0.99995), and Wesson's constant p_TEP ≡ J/M² = G/(2v_gal) = 1.52 × 10⁻¹⁵ cm² g⁻¹ s⁻¹ (J_obs/J_TEP = 1.11 ± 0.25).
